findings.title: Error-focused query check uses naive substring matching
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query string contains `event.type:error`. A negated query (`!event.type:error`), a mixed query (`event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`), or a quoted literal (`message:"event.type:error"`) all satisfy this check. For Discover, that makes `count()` get rewritten to `upsampled_count()`/`sum(sample_weight)` for rows that are not error events; transaction rows may not have meaningful sample_weight, leading to incorrect counts or Snuba errors. Parse the actual query terms (and handle negation/quotes) instead of substring matching.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses request query rather than executed query
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives the actual `query` being executed, but `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` only inspects `request.GET["query"]` inside `_is_error_focused_query` for the Discover dataset. In `get_event_stats_factory`, dashboard widget discover-split paths call `_get_event_stats` with rewritten queries such as `errors_only_query` (`... AND !event.type:transaction`) or `transactions_only_query` (`... AND event.type:transaction`). The helper can therefore decide an error-only split is not error-focused (undercounting) or decide a transaction-only split is error-focused (applying sample_weight to transactions). Pass the actual `query` string to the eligibility helper or derive the dataset/event type from the query being executed.

findings.title: Accidental submodule/gitlink committed
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink/submodule entry pointing at commit `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`. There is no related `.gitmodules` change and no code uses it; this looks accidental. Committing a submodule tracking the base commit can make clones fail or leave the working tree dirty and should be removed before merge.

findings.title: Transaction event not flushed before Snuba query
findings.body: In `test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events`, a transaction is stored via `self.store_event(...)` after the setUp wait calls, but no `wait_for_event_count` is issued for it before the API request. Snuba indexing is asynchronous, so `data[0][1][0]["count"] == 1` can race and fail. Wait for the transaction to be indexed (for example `self.wait_for_event_count(self.project.id, 2)`) before querying.
